title: Ad frequency: how often people should see your ad

facts.fact: Meta's brand-lift analysis found that a cap of 2 impressions per person per week captured 95% of the potential purchase-intent lift.
facts.quote: Meta’s brand-lift analysis found a cap of 2 impressions per person per week captured 95% of the potential purchase-intent lift.

facts.fact: Meta's effective frequency study found that a cap of 1 per week captured up to 80% of the total potential lift in ad recall.
facts.quote: A cap of 1 per week captured up to 80% of the total potential lift in ad recall.

facts.fact: In Meta's effective frequency study, purchase-intent lift did not start to slow until close to 1.5 impressions per week.
facts.quote: purchase-intent lift didn’t start to slow until close to 1.5 per week

facts.fact: In an MNTN CTV study reported by Epom, recall rose from about 64% after one view to 92% after six views in a single session.
facts.quote: recall rose from about 64% after one view to 92% after six in a single session

facts.fact: In the MNTN CTV study reported by Epom, purchase intent fell 16% over the same one-to-six view range.
facts.quote: purchase intent fell 16% over the same range

facts.fact: Epom suggests a starting cap of 4 to 6 ad views per viewer per week for CTV and streaming TV.
facts.quote: CTV / streaming TV | 4 to 6 per viewer

facts.fact: Epom suggests a starting cap of 3 to 5 per user per week for Facebook and Instagram Feed.
Epom suggests a starting cap of 2 to 4 per user per week for Facebook and Instagram Stories and Reels.
facts.quote: Facebook and Instagram Stories and Reels | 2 to 4

facts.fact: Epom suggests a starting cap of about 10 per user per week for programmatic online video.
Epom suggests a starting cap of 15 to 25 per user per week for prospecting display ads.
Epom suggests a starting cap of 10 to 15 per user per week for retargeting display ads, with about 3 a day at most.
facts.quote: Display, retargeting | 10 to 15 (about 3 a day at most)

facts.fact: Epom states that ad fatigue commonly sets in around 6 to 7 exposures on a single Facebook Feed creative.
facts.quote: Fatigue commonly sets in around 6 to 7 on a single creative

facts.fact: Improvado gives an example of a recency cap of one impression per hour in programmatic advertising.
facts.quote: Improvado gives a programmatic example of a recency cap: one impression per hour.

facts.fact: Improvado gives an example in which a cap of 3 per day on Google and 3 per day on Facebook can still mean 6 impressions a day for the same person.
facts.quote: a cap of 3 per day on Google and 3 per day on Facebook can still mean 6 impressions a day

facts.fact: Improvado defines an impression as each time an ad is displayed on a screen, whether or not the person noticed it.
facts.quote: defines an impression as each time an ad is displayed on a screen, whether or not the person noticed it

facts.fact: The page cites a popular rule that people must see an ad three times, which it advises readers to be skeptical of.
facts.quote: the popular rule that people must see an ad three times
